The test image shows a corn ear with dense white/grayish mold covering a cluster of kernels in the mid-ear region. Some green tinge is visible at the top of the affected area. Kernels beneath appear tan/discolored.

Key features: white cottony mold, clustered kernels affected (not strictly tip or base), possible greenish component.

Top candidates: Fusarium, Ear_rots_Gibberella, Ear_rots_Diplodia, Ear_rots_Trichoderma, Ear_rots_General_Mixed.

## Analysis

**Test image observations:**
- Corn ear affected
- Dense white/gray-white cottony mold covering a cluster of kernels in the mid-ear area
- Yellow healthy kernels visible around the affected cluster
- Kernels beneath the mold appear tan/discolored
- Slight greenish tinge at the top of the mold mass
- Not starting exclusively at the tip or base

**Reference comparison:**
- **Fusarium**: Top-right panel shows white cottony mold on clustered corn kernels with yellow kernels surrounding — very strong match to test image
- **Ear_rots_Gibberella**: Reference shows dark/brown husks; pink-red mold at tip — not matching
- **Ear_rots_General_Mixed**: Brown/black rotted kernels with some green areas — not matching
- **Ear_rots_Trichoderma**: Dark green mold — not matching (test image is predominantly white)
- **Common_smut**: Fleshy galls — clearly not matching

**Decision**: The white cottony mold on clustered mid-ear kernels with surrounding healthy yellow kernels and tan discoloration of infected kernels is a textbook match for **Fusarium** ear rot. The slight greenish tinge may be incidental Trichoderma co-contamination, but the dominant presentation is white cottony mold consistent with Fusarium.
